confidence_notes: Six web searches were used: one for the RBA rate and five for Wellington food and drink prices. Restaurant, coffee, cocktail and wine figures rest on crowd-sourced or estimate-based cost-of-living sites and 2026 visitor guides, not official surveys. Sources broadly agree on the inexpensive meal (about NZ$25) and on cappuccino (about NZ$6). The mid-range meal for two varied widely, from about NZ$80 in older pages to about NZ$145 in a 2026 guide, so I weighted toward the 2026 figure but kept it a little lower. Beer is uncertain. One guide quoted NZ$16-18 a pint, while an older crowd-sourced figure was about NZ$13 for 500ml. Wellington venues often pour about 425ml, so I used a typical restaurant draught price. Cocktail and wine come from sparse sources, with cocktails about NZ$17-20 and wine about NZ$11-15 a glass, and I kept them consistent with the local beer price. NZD prices were converted to USD using an approximate NZD/USD rate of 0.59 that I assumed from general knowledge. I did not search for it. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Wellington. I did not search for accommodation prices or inspect any listings, so they are the least certain anchors. The RBA rate is the 18 Nov 2026 observation reported by the RBA search results. I did not open the RBA page directly, and one stale RBA result showing a different rate was ignored.
comparable_city_reasoning: Wellington is a high-cost New Zealand capital, with restaurant prices about 10% above the national average in the sources found. It is comparable to Melbourne and Sydney for dining and bars but slightly cheaper for mid-range accommodation. Hostel and hotel anchors reflect a compact capital with steady business and government demand and limited budget hotel supply.
